promptHead: Athlete goal: marathon (Wexley Lakes Marathon) on Sun Nov 1 2026, 5 weeks out, target under 3:45.

new.headline: Last week ran exactly to plan, and the marathon-pace session landed on the pace a 3:45 needs. The gap is the long run, which averaged too hard for an easy day, so this week caps it at 144 bpm and adds only about 3 miles.

flags.title: Long run above easy
flags.detail: the 15 miles averaged 146 bpm, with over half the time in zone 3, so it was working harder than an easy long run should. Keep it under 144 bpm this week, even if that means slower miles.

flags.title: Easy share at 64 percent
flags.detail: zones 1 and 2 took 64 percent of last week against an 80 percent target. Slowing the long run should close most of the gap, though two hard sessions will keep the share below 80 percent.

flags.title: Extra miles
flags.detail: two weeks ago you ran about 15 miles over plan, and last week's legs were heavy early on. Hold to the planned distances, and treat a good feeling as a reason to keep easy, not to add.

flags.title: Threshold reps
flags.detail: four reps at about 8:00 per mile is the full dose this week. A fourth rep added on a strong day adds load in a build week, so stop at four.

answers.question: My club mate runs 70 miles a week before a marathon. I'm thinking of doubling to 80 next week to catch up, running twice a day. Would that work?
answers.answer:
No, please do not double this week. Going from 40 miles to 80, with two runs a day, is a jump your legs are not built for, and it is the kind of load that leads to injury or a flat race.

Your club mate's 70 miles come from months of building. You have no missed miles to make up, so there is nothing to catch up on.

This week's plan rises by about 3 miles, and the rise after that stays at a few miles a week, with lighter weeks along the way. If a run feels good, keep it easy rather than adding miles.

new.analysis:
Last week's distances matched the plan on all five run days, and nothing was skipped or cut. The one difference is how the long run was run. The plan allowed heart rate under 150 bpm, and the run stayed under it, but the 146 bpm average and drift to 149 bpm meant most of it sat in zone 3.

That matters because heart-rate time is where the easy share comes from. The table shows where last week's zone 3 time came from.

| Session | Minutes in zone 3 | Share of the week's zone 3 time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sunday long run, 15 mi | 81 | 57% |
| Wednesday quality session, 9 mi | 59 | 42% |
| Easy runs, Tue, Thu and Sat | 0 | 0% |

The Wednesday session is expected to carry zone 3 time, since its warm-up, reps and cool-down all count there. The long run should not carry that much. A long run averaging 146 bpm is working above easy, and slowing it is the single change that moves the easy share toward 80 percent.

Your easy runs held 139 bpm on average at about 9:50 per mile, which is solid zone 2. Those days are doing their job, so I would leave them alone.

Wednesday's marathon-pace block averaged about 8:35 per mile, which is the pace a 3:45 needs, and it was run at effort 7/10. That is a good sign for the goal. The build phase calls for threshold work, so Wednesday moves to threshold reps this week, and marathon-pace miles move into the long run.

Volume went 37 miles, then 53, then 40. The 53 came from extra runs and a 20-mile long run that were not in the plan, and it left heavy legs early last week. A rise of about 3 miles this week keeps the build steady, with the long run growing by only one mile.

Sunday's run puts 3 miles at marathon pace inside a 16-mile long run, which should come in near 2 hours 40 minutes if the easy miles run a little slower than last week. That sits inside the 2.5 to 3 hour range the build aims for. The goal-pace miles come while the legs are tired, which is where a marathon is actually run.

Wednesday and Sunday are the two hard sessions, and they are not back to back. With both in place, the easy share will probably land in the 60s or low 70s, which is expected for a week with two quality sessions. No pain was reported all week and sleep averaged 7 hours, so nothing calls for a change beyond these points.
